the mechanisms that regulate the release of the parathyroid hormone.

the effects of cGMP on Ca2+-activated K+ channels are complex.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parathyroid cells express a voltage-insensitive, high-[Ca2+]-activated cation conductance.
Ca2+-sensitive cation channels are modulated by Ca2+-sensitizing receptors and by intracellular cAMP.

Ca2+-sensitive cation channels are present in parathyroid cell membrane and that these channels may play a role, along with voltage-gated Ca2+channels, in regulating parathyroid cell secretion and Ca2+ homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cAMP can regulate ion fluxes through Ca2+-conductance channels.
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation regulates Ca2+-sensitive cation channels in parathyroid gland cells.
